findings.title: Missing React key for GrafanaRuleListItem in filtered list
findings.body: FilterViewResults maps rules to list items and computes a unique key for each rule, but in the origin === 'grafana' branch the returned GrafanaRuleListItem does not receive a key prop. React will emit missing-key warnings and may reconcile list items by position, which can cause wrong or retained component state, such as open dropdowns or silence drawers, when the filtered list updates.

findings.title: Silence action is shown but does nothing for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
findings.body: The new list item supplies only promRule to RuleActionsButtons, so rule is undefined. AlertRuleMenu can still render 'Silence notifications' because canSilence includes Grafana Prometheus rule abilities. Clicking it sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is only rendered when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. With no ruler rule the drawer never appears, so the Silence action is dead UI.

findings.title: Delete and pause actions are hidden for prom-only Grafana rules despite computed abilities
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu computes canDelete and canPause from both ruler abilities and Grafana Prometheus abilities, but the Delete menu item is guarded by rulerRule and the Pause item requires a Grafana ruler rule. In the new alert list view Grafana rules are rendered from Prometheus data without a ruler rule, so users who have delete or pause permission according to the new Grafana abilities will not see these actions. Delete appears especially likely to be intended because the delete modal can be opened from the rule identifier alone.

findings.title: skipToken does not disable Grafana Prometheus rule abilities
findings.body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities converts skipToken to undefined, but useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still produces real abilities. In particular, Duplicate is allowed when the user has Grafana alert-rule create permission, regardless of the actual rule. Because AlertRuleMenu ORs these abilities with ruler abilities, this can show Duplicate for non-Grafana, missing, or plugin-provided rules where the Grafana hook should be inert.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false, replacing the previous isFederatedRuleGroup check. Federated ruler rule groups should be immutable, but this change makes update, delete, pause, and restore appear supported for them if the user has permissions, regressing UI/RBAC behavior for federated cloud rules.

findings.title: Abilities memo is invalidated by a new canSilence tuple each render
findings.body: useCanSilence returns a new [supported, allowed] array on every render, and that tuple is included in the useMemo dependency array of useAllRulerRuleAbilities. The memo therefore recomputes on every render, which can add noticeable overhead when these hooks are invoked for many rows in the rule list.

findings.title: Extra closing brace in Grafana rule key
findings.body: getGrafanaRuleKey returns a template string ending in ${rule.uid}}, so the generated key contains an unintended trailing closing brace. This does not crash React but makes keys incorrect and can confuse debugging or key-based assumptions.

findings.title: Clipboard write promise rejection is not handled
findings.body: copyToClipboard calls navigator.clipboard.writeText(...).then(...) without a catch handler. If the Clipboard API rejects, for example due to browser permissions or an insecure context, the result is an unhandled promise rejection.

findings.title: RuleDetails RBAC tests assert contradictory behavior
findings.body: Tests named 'Should not render Edit/Delete button for users with the update/delete permission' mock useIsRuleEditable with isEditable or isRemovable true and then assert the buttons are absent, without granting the corresponding permissions. This likely tests the wrong condition and can pass even if the RBAC button visibility logic is broken.
